page: Microsoft Azure D64plds_v5 is an ARM64-based virtual machine powered by an Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 64 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.0 GHz with a single thread per core. The memory configuration consists of 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. For local storage, the server includes 2458 GB of local disk capacity and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not feature any GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench software compilation with Clang scoring in the top 25%. Cached small-block read-only memory bandwidth is also highly performant at 4384.56 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with Geekbench single-core and text processing benchmarks falling into the bottom 25%. Large-block uncached memory read and write speeds, static web serving throughput, and database operations perform in the average tier.

Given its ARM architecture and high physical core count, the D64plds_v5 offers a cost-efficient profile for multi-threaded workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores without hyper-threading. The low memory-to-core ratio makes it less suitable for memory-intensive databases, but highly effective for scale-out compute tasks. Recommended workloads include multi-threaded software compilation, Redis key-value stores, web serving, and moderate-scale parallel processing tasks.
